text:
Cam Fowler is still logging big minutes for St. Louis, more than 21 a night, but the points have stopped. He has gone ten straight games without one, and his season sits at 4 assists in 17 games. Last season, his first full one with the Blues, he had 30 points.

The blank isn't only bad luck. The Blues have scored 5.4 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, which usually evens out, but the chances themselves have thinned: 8.3 expected goals with him on over the last ten games, against 10.1 usual (expected goals measure the quality of chances). His ice time is down 1:40 a night over that stretch too.

At 34, he still moves well; his speed bursts rank in the 88th percentile. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking liked his puck movement last season, with 56% of his exits leaving the zone with possession. The worry is at the other end: Evolving-Hockey had opponents creating more chances with him on than with almost any other defenseman (bottom 6%). We'd watch his minutes. If they keep sliding, the Blues are telling you something.
headline: Cam Fowler's ten-game blank
